key_insight: A performance-portable GPU + distributed-memory + high-order time-integration strategy makes large 3D phase-field precipitate simulations faster than real time.
engineering_relevance: This enables application-scale microstructure prediction for materials design, large simulation ensembles, and potential real-time support for experiments on exascale systems.
method: Used MEUMAPPS C++ with performance-portable GPU computing and large-scale distributed-memory parallelism.
Applied Fourier pseudospectral phase-field simulation with high-order implicit-explicit time integration.
Demonstrated on a 1.5-billion-grid-point Ni-Nb-Fe precipitate aging case.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a seven-hour heat treatment completed in 5.5 hours, up to 17.5x single-node GPU speedup, near-ideal strong scaling to 4096 GPUs, and 2.6–2.9x gain from fourth-order time integration.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on access to leadership-class GPU systems and careful tuning of solver accuracy, communication, and memory traffic.
paper_title: Accelerating phase-field simulations on exascale computing systems for faster-than-real-time precipitate aging predictions
